01 / CLASSIC EDITOR

Every parameter,
as the panel names them.

The DX7's own list, in its own units and groups, with the panel's gestures: pick an operator, switch operators off to hear one layer, copy an envelope, and compare against the voice you started from. The small number on each row is the numbered button that parameter sits on in the DX7's edit mode. Nothing here is measured or searched — what you set is exactly what your synth gets.

Switching back to Interactive makes this edited voice the starting voice, with every slider at 0.

CLIP

Click the grid to place a note, click it again to clear it. The velocity row sets how hard each step is played; hold extends the note before it. The loop keeps playing while you edit, so you hear changes as you make them. It is never saved into a patch.
CHORD LAB
PROGRESSION—
SELECTED CHORD—

UNDER THIS PATCH

Four stacked carriers clip where one does not. This renders every chord through the current patch and reports what the mix peaks at, so a voicing can be chosen on a number rather than a guess.

Click a chord on the wheel to add it to the progression. The seven lit chords are the ones in the key; the rest are drawn for context. The chord row under the pattern puts a chord on a step — click a step to move it through the progression and back to none. A step with a chord plays that chord instead of its own note.
